issue: Distractor (b) explanation teaches a wrong rule: it says 'Disclosure is for remote cases.' Under ASC 470-10-45-2, when acceleration under a subjective acceleration clause is remote, neither reclassification nor disclosure is required; disclosure alone applies to the middle case (acceleration reasonably possible). The item-level explanation also gives only the 'probable' tier.
evidence: Choice (b) explanation: 'Disclosure is for remote cases.' ASC 470-10-45-2: some circumstances (recurring losses, liquidity problems) call for current classification; others call only for disclosure of the clause; 'Neither reclassification nor disclosure would be required if the likelihood of the acceleration of the due date were remote.' Key (d) Current is right.
fix: Rewrite (b) explanation: 'Disclosure alone applies when acceleration is reasonably possible but not probable; if it is remote, neither reclassification nor disclosure is needed. Here acceleration is probable, so the debt is current.' Expand the item explanation to state all three tiers (probable: current; reasonably possible: disclose; remote: nothing).

issue: Six practice items (21% of the module's 28) test topics that this lesson never teaches, and no other FAR lesson teaches them either: debt with detachable warrants (dbt-14), convertible debt at issuance and on conversion after ASU 2020-06 (dbt-15, dbt-19), derecognition only on payment or legal release / in-substance defeasance (dbt-26), line-of-credit issuance costs (dbt-27) and subjective acceleration clauses (dbt-28). A learner who misses them is routed to a lesson with nothing to read.
evidence: Lesson headings: Notes payable at present value; Current or noncurrent?; Extinguishment; Disclosures; Debt covenant compliance; Modification, extinguishment and TDRs. grep -i 'detachable|convertible|defeas|subjective|line.of.credit|revolv' over content/far/modules/*/lesson.md finds only EPS if-converted text (far-eps) and 'readily convertible' (far-cash, far-ratios). far-bonds lesson (prerequisite) covers pricing, effective interest, issuance costs and between-dates issuance only, although far-bond-15/-26/-27 also test convertibles and warrants.
fix: Add a short section 'Other debt topics' (here, or in far-bonds with dbt-14/15/19 moved there) teaching: (1) bonds with detachable warrants: allocate by relative fair values when both are known, incremental method when only one is; (2) convertible debt after ASU 2020-06: all proceeds to debt unless a derivative or substantial premium; conversion per original terms moves the carrying amount to equity with no gain or loss; (3) debt is derecognized only when paid or legally released, so in-substance defeasance leaves the debt on the books; (4) line-of-credit costs may be deferred as an asset and amortized ratably; (5) subjective acceleration clauses: probable acceleration means current, reasonably possible means disclose, remote means nothing. Add one inline check and a flashcard.

issue: Pure-recall items are labeled skill 'analysis' with difficulty 3, which is two levels off. Each asks for a single rule stated directly by the facts (in-substance defeasance keeps the debt on the books; revolver costs may be an asset; probable acceleration means current), with no computation and no interrelationships to examine. This inflates the module's analysis share, which feeds the Blueprint skill-mix targets.
evidence: dbt-26: 'places risk-free securities in an irrevocable trust... isn't legally released. What is the accounting?' dbt-27: 'costs to obtain a revolving line of credit with nothing drawn. How are the costs presented?' dbt-28: 'subjective acceleration clause, and acceleration is probable. How is it classified?' Compare dbt-05 and dbt-15 (same kind of recall), which are labeled remembering, difficulty 1.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions (Remembering and Understanding vs Analysis); content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel dbt-26, dbt-27 and dbt-28 as skill 'remembering', difficulty 1 (dbt-28 could be 2 once the three-tier rule is taught).

issue: Application-level items are labeled 'analysis' (mostly difficulty 3), one level off. Each applies one stated rule or one or two arithmetic steps. The clearest case: dbt-23 and dbt-24 are the same computations as dbt-01 and dbt-02 (PV of a 2-year noninterest-bearing note, then Year-1 effective interest), yet they are labeled analysis/3 while dbt-01 and dbt-02 are application/2.
evidence: dbt-23: 100,000/1.10^2 = 82,645 (analysis, 3) vs dbt-01: 200,000/1.08^2 = 171,468 (application, 2). dbt-24: 82,645 x 10% (analysis, 3) vs dbt-02: 171,468 x 8% (application, 2). dbt-21: 110,000 - 90,000 = 20,000 gain. dbt-22 and dbt-16: two subtractions. dbt-18 and dbt-25: apply the grace-period / more-than-one-year waiver rule. dbt-03: apply ASC 470-10-45-15. fix: Relabel dbt-03, 16, 18, 21, 22, 23, 24 and 25 as 'application'. Set difficulty 2 for 23/24 (to match 01/02) and 18/21/25. Then add genuine analysis-level items or a TBS (see the pedagogy finding).

issue: Distractor (a) '$40,000 loss' is explained as 'This ignores the premium', but ignoring the premium gives a $40,000 GAIN, which is choice (c), and (c)'s rationale ('compares the price with face only') describes that same error. The rationale for (a) names an error that does not produce (a)'s number. Its partial-computation trap label is wrong too.
evidence: Ignore premium: 2,000,000 - 1,960,000 = +40,000 gain (choice c). A $40,000 loss needs that error plus a sign reversal (or reading 98 as 102: 2,040,000 - 2,040,000 = 0, so that is not it either). Key: 2,040,000 - 1,960,000 = 80,000 gain (d), confirmed.
fix: Either relabel (a) as 'Ignores the premium and reverses the sign (treats paying below face as a loss)' with trap wrong-sign, or replace (a) with 'No gain or loss' (subtracts the $40,000 premium as if it were a discount: 1,960,000 - 1,960,000 = 0; trap wrong-sign).

issue: For three distractors, the stem cannot produce the number, or the rationale doesn't name the error that does. dbt-13 (b) $220,000 needs a discount rate (about 10%) that the stem never gives. dbt-21 (d) $10,000 cannot be derived from 110,000 and 90,000, and is explained only as 'Not the computation.' dbt-23 (d) $80,000 is the simple-interest discount (100,000 - 2 x 10% x 100,000), but its rationale just says 'Not the computation.'
evidence: dbt-13: 550,000 - 400,000/1.10^2 = 219,421, about 220,000, but only at an unstated 10%; no rate appears in the stem. dbt-21: no pairing of 110,000 and 90,000 gives 10,000 (110-90 = 20; 90/9 = 10 is not meaningful). dbt-23: 100,000 x (1 - 0.10 x 2) = 80,000.

issue: Answer cue. issue: Four trap labels don't match the misconception their distractors model.
evidence: dbt-10 (d) 'Equity increases' is labeled irrelevant-fact, but the stem has no irrelevant fact; the error is wrong-rule. dbt-14 (c) $10,000 is labeled wrong-classification, but it is the incremental (residual) method, i.e. wrong-rule: 1,000,000 - 990,000. dbt-21 (b) 'No gain; reduce future interest' is labeled wrong-classification, but it applies the wrong branch of the 470-60 test, i.e. wrong-rule. dbt-24 (b) $17,355 is labeled wrong-classification, but it takes the whole discount (100,000 - 82,645) in Year 1, i.e. wrong-period.

issue: The stem says only 'A debtor settles $100,000 of debt by transferring land'. It never states financial difficulty or a creditor concession, yet the key reads '$30,000 TDR gain' and the explanation calls it a restructuring. Without those facts the transaction is an ordinary extinguishment under 470-50 (same numbers, different label), so the key asserts a classification the stem doesn't support.
evidence: Compare dbt-16 ('A debtor in difficulty settles...') and dbt-13 ('A debtor in financial difficulty...'). The numbers are the same either way: 100,000 - 70,000 = 30,000 gain on settlement; 70,000 - 50,000 = 20,000 gain on the land.
fix: Add 'A debtor in financial difficulty... the creditor accepts land in full settlement' to the stem, or change the key text to '$30,000 gain on settlement of the debt; $20,000 gain on the land'.

issue: calc is true, but no computation is needed: the answer is the equipment's stated fair value ($90,000). The stem's 'At what amount is the note recorded?' could also be read as asking for the face amount (a gross-method note at $100,000 with a $10,000 discount).
evidence: Key (a) $90,000 = the fair value given in the stem; no arithmetic. Under the gross method, Notes payable is credited at 100,000 and Discount on notes payable is debited 10,000.
source: ASC 835-30-25-10; schema calc semantics (set only when a computation is needed)
fix: Set calc false and difficulty 1, and ask 'At what net carrying amount is the note initially reported?'. Or make it computational: ask for the discount and the implied effective rate (100,000/90,000 = 1.1111, so about 5.41% a year), or for Year-1 interest expense.

issue: The lesson states the classification rules incompletely. (1) Refinancing: it omits that the entity must intend to refinance; that a post-balance-sheet issuance of equity securities also qualifies; and the conditions a financing agreement must meet (it doesn't expire or isn't callable within one year, it isn't cancelable by the lender, no violation exists, the lender is able to honor it). The lesson only says 'qualifying', and chk1 relies on those conditions in its stem. (2) Callable debt: the waiver must run 'for more than one year (or operating cycle, if longer)', but the lesson and takeaways drop the operating-cycle alternative. Flashcard fc2 has the same gaps.
evidence: Lesson: 'refinance it long-term, or sign a qualifying non-cancelable financing agreement'; takeaway: 'waives the right for more than one year'. ASC 470-10-45-14: intent plus ability demonstrated by (a) a post-BS-date issuance of a long-term obligation or equity securities, or (b) a financing agreement meeting 45-14(b)(1)-(3). ASC 470-10-45-11(a): 'for more than one year (or operating cycle, if longer)'. fc2 back: 'actual long-term refinancing or a qualifying financing agreement'.
fix: Add to the 'Refinancing traps' list: intent is required; equity securities also qualify; a qualifying agreement doesn't expire within one year, isn't cancelable by the lender, has no violations, and the lender can honor it; the noncurrent amount is capped at the amount available (a reasonable estimate of the minimum if it fluctuates). Add '(or operating cycle, if longer)' to the callable-debt rule. Update fc2 to match.

issue: Rounding in the worked example: the work line shows 150,000 x 0.77218, which is 115,827, not the 115,828 shown. A learner recomputing from the factor gets a different figure.

The modification/extinguishment and TDR section leaves out commonly tested details. Fees paid to the lender are included in the new-terms cash flows for the 10% test. Third-party costs are expensed on a modification but capitalized as issuance costs of the new debt on an extinguishment. A debtor TDR can also be settled by granting an equity interest (measured at its fair value).
evidence: The lesson covers lender fees for each outcome and the asset-transfer and modification-of-terms TDRs only.
fix: Add one line each: 'The 10% test includes fees paid to or received from the lender in the new cash flows'; 'Third-party costs: expensed on a modification, deferred with the new debt on an extinguishment'; 'TDR by granting equity: credit equity at the fair value of the shares; gain = carrying amount - fair value of the equity'.
